b:
My Tamil of Kumari,
who garlanded religion and caste,
cooked up valour
to seize a stranger's land,
lost your possessions
and lost your rights too:

seeing the path we lived
and the path of life
become the burnt pages
of a paper book,
I stood troubled

I asked: what way is there out of suffering?
"When trouble comes, laugh," said
Valluvar, the dark-skinned one,
now painted in saffron

The empty smiles could not
build a fence
against my sorrows
that rushed past like a jungle flood

The modern Krishna,
playing with the gopis in his garden,
laughs too,
"eternal bliss!",
in his Kailasa-Dwaraka

Once
reason
made the man who could only bow
to the temple tower at the gate
step across the temple threshold….

Today
fascism
plays dice
with it

And even Lord Shiva there
is a mere spectator

The sites of mosques
shine as graveyards,
and along with them, a statue

Rama's arrows
turned into arrows of blood

To save
his churches blazing in flames,
even prayers were not enough
for that God

Should not the blood
spilled by Syrian refugees
have turned to fire
and become a fortress?

And why
this partiality
between Kannagi
and Draupadi?

Among the many flowers
that bloomed at the Buddha's holy feet,
a red lotus:
let Tamil search for a simile
for whether they bathed in blood

Let the rutting elephants
that wrestle
over religion,
caste,
language
and race
perish and be destroyed

But
could God not at least
lend an ear
to the cries
of the little ants
caught and crushed
between their legs?

Back then
Asifa
was destroyed
in that God's
own house

The mother who gave the milk of wisdom
to a crying child
did not appear for her

The one who worked a wonder in the sky
for children tending sheep
did not end her agony either

If that is your God,
let it stay with you

To bring my burnt pages back to life
I do not need that God
note: "Tamil of Kumari" recalls Kumari Kandam, the legendary lost Tamil homeland to the south. "When trouble comes, laugh" is Thirukkural 621; the saffron refers to recent images of Thiruvalluvar dressed in saffron. "Kailasa" is the self-declared nation of the godman Nithyananda. The man at the temple tower recalls the temple-entry movement inspired by Periyar's rationalism. Kannagi burned Madurai with her anger, while Draupadi was left to be humiliated. The mother who gave "the milk of wisdom" is Parvati, who fed the child saint Sambandar; the wonder in the sky for shepherd children is the Marian apparition at Fatima. Asifa Bano, an eight-year-old nomad girl who grazed her family's animals, was raped and murdered inside a temple in Kathua, India, in 2018.
